title: Verizon Q3 2026 Earnings Beat Estimates as Phone Adds Hit Five-Year High; Guidance Raised
headline: Verizon Q3 2026 Earnings Beat Estimates as Phone Adds Hit Five-Year High; Guidance Raised
subheadline: Adjusted EPS rose 8.3% to $1.31 on revenue of $34.31 billion; Verizon added 406,000 postpaid phone subscribers and lifted its full-year EPS outlook to $5.04-$5.06.
body:
• Verizon's third-quarter adjusted earnings rose 8.3% year over year to $1.31 per share, beating the $1.27 consensus, while revenue rose 1.5% to $34.31 billion and missed the $34.81 billion estimate.
  • The carrier added 406,000 postpaid phone subscribers — up more than 820% from a year earlier and its strongest third quarter in five years — plus 137,000 postpaid accounts, its best quarterly account growth in over a decade.
  • Adjusted EBITDA rose 8% to a record $13.80 billion and free cash flow rose 12.1% to $7.8 billion, as service revenue grew 3.5% and equipment revenue fell 9% on lower upgrades and reduced handset subsidies.
  • Verizon raised its full-year 2026 guidance for the third straight quarter: adjusted EPS of $5.04 to $5.06 and postpaid phone net additions of 1.1 million to 1.2 million.

Verizon Communications beat earnings expectations for the third quarter on Monday and raised its full-year outlook for the third consecutive quarter, as its strongest wireless customer growth in five years and tighter cost discipline more than offset a revenue miss and falling handset sales. The results marked one year under chief executive Dan Schulman and the company's multi-year transformation plan.

Adjusted earnings per share increased 8.3% year over year to $1.31, ahead of the $1.27 Zacks consensus estimate, according to Zacks. Total operating revenue rose 1.5% to $34.31 billion, below the $34.81 billion consensus. On a reported basis, net income rose 5.2% to about $5.3 billion, or $1.25 per share, compared with $1.17 a year earlier, with a net income margin of 15.5%, up from 14.9%. Operating income rose 6.7% to $8.65 billion.

Phone Additions Surge, Churn Falls

Customer growth was the headline. Verizon delivered 406,000 postpaid phone net additions in the quarter ended September 30, compared with just 44,000 a year earlier, and added 137,000 postpaid accounts. Postpaid phone churn improved four basis points to 0.94%, with consumer churn at 0.87%. Promotional acquisition costs fell 41% and retention costs improved 30%, as gains built on Simplicity offers and its loyalty program, rather than heavy subsidies, brought in higher-value customers.

"Verizon delivered another record-breaking quarter. One year into our transformation, Verizon is fundamentally stronger — operationally, financially, and competitively."

— Dan Schulman, Verizon CEO

Broadband added 314,000 connections — 159,000 fixed wireless and 155,000 fiber — taking total broadband connections to 17.4 million. Verizon still expects fiber passings to exceed 32 million by year-end, toward 40 million to 50 million over the medium term.

Service Growth Offsets Equipment Weakness

Service revenues and other rose 3.5% to $29.20 billion. Mobility and broadband service revenue reached $23.5 billion, up 2.9% year over year, accelerating from 2.8% growth in the second quarter and 1.6% in the first. Wireless equipment revenue fell 9% to $5.12 billion, which the company attributed in its third-quarter release to significantly lower upgrade volumes as customers keep devices longer, and to its strategic decision to reduce spending on device subsidies.

By segment, consumer revenue rose 1.3% to $26.43 billion and business revenue rose 2.6% to $7.02 billion. Total operating expenses fell 0.2%, and adjusted EBITDA rose 8% to a record $13.80 billion, with the margin expanding 240 basis points to 40.2%.

Cash Flow, AI Fiber Deal and Raised Guidance

Third-quarter free cash flow rose 12.1% to $7.8 billion, taking the nine-month total to $18.01 billion. Verizon returned $12.8 billion to shareholders in the first nine months — $8.8 billion in dividends and $4.0 billion in share repurchases — and still expects up to $4.5 billion of buybacks for the full year. Net unsecured debt stood at $123.72 billion, or 2.3 times adjusted EBITDA.

The company also signed an agreement valued at more than $2 billion with Amazon Web Services to scale distributed computing for AI workloads. For the full year, Verizon now expects adjusted EPS of $5.04 to $5.06, implying 7% to 7.5% growth, up from 6% to 7% previously. It raised its postpaid phone forecast to 1.1 million to 1.2 million, expects mobility and broadband service revenue growth in the upper half of its 2.5% to 3% range, and expects free cash flow growth approaching 12%. Capital expenditure guidance was unchanged at $16 billion to $16.5 billion.
